newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Thailand soaks up naphtha glut.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Thailand soaks up naphtha glut.

text.p: Brisk buying from Thailand has absorbed excess naphtha barrels and pushed the market back into backwardation, while the low Taiwan reformate award has put a dampener on the gasoline market, traders said on Thursday.
Naphtha in Japan dipped back into backwardation after a surplus of prompt supplies had kept the market in contango since late April.
Singapore naphtha swaps for August and September slipped into a backwardation of around 5 cents a barrel from being quoted at par on Wednesday.
August was quoted firmer at $21.10/$21.20 and September at $21.05/$21.15.

In Japan, first half August open-spec cargoes were valued 50 cents per tonne higher than first-half September cargoes. Half month September spreads moved into a 25 cent backwardation after being talked at par on Wednesday.
Traders in Singapore said at least six MR (30,000-tonne) cargoes from the Mediterranean have been sold into Thailand for prompt delivery between July 4 and August 2.

Traders in Japan also said naphtha's recovery was due to the return of north Asian petrochemicals from spring turnarounds and support from importers with Mideast term supplies who prefer to load cargoes in a backwardated market.
In Singapore, one trader was seeking a full naphtha cargo of open-spec quality for second-half August lifting at around 50-60 cents per barrel over spot quotes, fob.
But sellers held off indications in the fast-recovering market.
The sentiment in the gasoline market was, in comparison, bearish on news of the low Taiwanese import tender award.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) awarded just one 250,000-barrel cargo of 95-octane unleaded reformate at $23.30 per barrel, c+f Taiwan August 11-20, a company official said.
"The price is very good," he said. "But we only bought one cargo as the other sellers could not meet this price."
The award was much lower than CPC's last tender, for August 1-10 arrival, which awarded two cargoes to a Dutch trader at around $24.60-$24.76 per barrel, cost-and-freight, sources said.
"It is very suicidal," said a trader in Singapore. "Prices in Singapore are already very low."

In Singapore, 50,000-barrels of unleaded 95-octane lifting August 4-8, was offered by a Japanese trader at $23.00 per barrel, fob, and later at $22.80, both times facing another Japanese buyer matching the offer. But no deal was concluded, the buyer said.
On Wednesday, the grade was offered of $22.90.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
